api_documentation_examples.title: RESTful API Endpoint Documentation

poor_example.content:
POST /users
Creates a user.
Returns user object.

good_example.description: Creates a new user account with the specified details. Requires admin authentication.

email.description: User's email address. Must be unique.

username.description: Unique username. Alphanumeric and underscores only.

password.description: User password. Must contain uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character.

role.description: User role. Defaults to 'user' if not specified.

body.message: Admin access required to create users
An unexpected error occurred. Please try again later.

good_example.example_request:
curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/users \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGc..." \
  -d '{
    "email": "user@example.com",
    "username": "john_doe_42",
    "password": "SecureP@ss123",
    "full_name": "John Doe",
    "role": "user"
  }'
notes: Email verification email is sent asynchronously after user creation
Password is hashed using bcrypt before storage (never stored in plain text)
Username cannot be changed after creation
Rate limit: 100 requests per hour per IP address

best_practices: Include all possible response codes with examples
Specify required vs optional fields clearly
Document validation rules (min/max length, regex patterns)
Note any side effects (emails sent, webhooks triggered)
Specify rate limits and authentication requirements

poor_example.content:
To schedule a report:
1. Click Reports
2. Click Schedule
3. Fill out the form
4. Click Save
issues: Assumes user knows where to find 'Reports'
No explanation of what happens after scheduling

good_example.title: How to Schedule Automated Reports
good_example.introduction: Scheduled reports allow you to automatically receive analytics data via email at regular intervals. This guide walks through creating your first scheduled report.
prerequisites: You need 'Report Manager' role or higher
At least one report template must exist in your workspace

steps.title: Navigate to Reports Dashboard
steps.instruction: From the main navigation menu on the left, click **Analytics**, then select **Reports** from the dropdown.
steps.tip: If you don't see the Reports option, you may not have the required permissions. Contact your workspace administrator.

steps.title: Create New Schedule
steps.instruction: In the top-right corner of the Reports page, click the **Schedule Report** button (calendar icon).

steps.title: Configure Report Settings
steps.instruction: Fill out the scheduling form with the following information:

sub_steps.instruction: Select which report to schedule from the dropdown. Use the search box if you have many templates.
Choose how often to receive the report: Daily, Weekly, Monthly, or Custom.

details.daily: Sent every day at specified time
details.weekly: Sent on selected day(s) of week
details.monthly: Sent on specified date each month (1-28)
details.custom: Use cron expression for advanced scheduling

sub_steps.instruction: Select the time to send the report (in your local timezone).
sub_steps.best_practice: Choose morning hours (6-9 AM) for reports you want to review daily.

sub_steps.instruction: Enter email addresses of recipients (comma-separated). You can add up to 10 recipients.
Select output format: PDF, Excel, or CSV.
sub_steps.guidance: PDF for stakeholder reports, Excel/CSV for data analysis

steps.title: Review and Save
steps.instruction: Review your settings, then click **Save Schedule**. You'll see a confirmation message and your new schedule will appear in the list.

steps.title: Verify First Delivery
steps.instruction: Your first report will be sent at the next scheduled time. Check the 'Next Run' column to see when that will be.
steps.note: To send a test report immediately, click the three-dot menu next to your schedule and select 'Send Now'.

what_happens_next: Reports are generated automatically at the scheduled time
All recipients receive an email with the report attached
Delivery history is logged and viewable under 'Schedule History'
Failed deliveries trigger automatic retries (3 attempts) and notify you

troubleshooting.problem: I don't receive the scheduled report
solutions: Verify your email address is spelled correctly in recipients list
Check Schedule History for error messages
Ensure the report template still exists and has data

troubleshooting.problem: Report is empty or shows no data
solutions: Verify date range filters in the report template
Check that you have data for the selected time period
Ensure data source permissions haven't changed

best_practices_for_user_guides: Explain WHY as well as HOW (best practices)

features.example:
## Features

✨ **Simple API** - Create charts with just 3 lines of code
📊 **12+ Chart Types** - Line, bar, pie, scatter, and more
🎨 **Fully Customizable** - Control every aspect of appearance
📱 **Responsive** - Works on mobile, tablet, and desktop
⚡ **Fast** - Render 100k data points in <100ms
🔧 **TypeScript Support** - Full type definitions included

readme_best_practices: Put most important info first (what it does, why use it)
Include a quick start that works copy-paste
Use badges for credibility (build status, downloads, version)
Add visuals (screenshots, GIFs, diagrams) - especially for UI libraries
Link to full documentation rather than cramming everything in README
Include installation instructions for all package managers
Show example code that actually runs
Keep it scannable with headings and bullet points

## System Overview

The E-Commerce Platform is a microservices-based architecture that handles product catalog, user management, order processing, and payment integration. The system is designed for:

- **Scale**: Handle 10,000 concurrent users
- **Reliability**: 99.9% uptime SLA
- **Security**: PCI DSS compliance for payment processing
- **Performance**: <200ms API response time (p95)

sections.content: [Include diagram showing: Frontend, API Gateway, Microservices, Databases, Message Queue, Cache Layer]

sections.example:
### API Gateway (Kong)

**Purpose**: Single entry point for all client requests. Handles authentication, rate limiting, and routing.

**Technology**: Kong API Gateway v3.0

**Responsibilities**:
- JWT token validation
- Rate limiting (100 req/min per user)
- Request routing to appropriate microservice
- CORS handling
- SSL termination

**Scalability**: Horizontally scalable, currently 3 instances behind load balancer

**Dependencies**: None (stateless)

sections.purpose: Explain how data moves through the system
sections.example:
### Order Placement Flow

1. User submits order via Web UI
2. Request hits API Gateway → validates JWT
3. Order Service receives request
   - Validates product availability (calls Inventory Service)
   - Calculates total (calls Pricing Service)
   - Creates order record in Orders DB
4. Order Service publishes 'OrderCreated' event to message queue
5. Payment Service consumes event → processes payment
6. Payment Service publishes 'PaymentProcessed' event
7. Fulfillment Service consumes event → creates shipping label
8. Email Service consumes event → sends order confirmation

[Include sequence diagram]

### Technology Choices

| Component | Technology | Justification |
|-----------|------------|---------------|
| Frontend | React 18 | Large ecosystem, good performance |
| API Gateway | Kong | Plugin ecosystem, high performance |
| Services | Node.js / Express | Team expertise, npm ecosystem |
| Database | PostgreSQL | ACID compliance, strong community |
| Cache | Redis | High performance, persistence options |
| Message Queue | RabbitMQ | Reliable, mature, good monitoring |
| Deployment | Kubernetes | Auto-scaling, self-healing |
| Monitoring | Prometheus + Grafana | Open source, powerful querying |

writing_improvement_exercises.title: Passive to Active Voice
writing_improvement_exercises.weak: The error was caused by incorrect configuration of the database connection string.
writing_improvement_exercises.strong: Incorrect database connection string caused the error.
writing_improvement_exercises.lesson: Active voice is more direct and clear. Use passive voice only when actor is unknown or irrelevant.

writing_improvement_exercises.title: Remove Jargon
writing_improvement_exercises.weak: Leverage the API endpoint to facilitate the creation of user entities in the persistence layer.
writing_improvement_exercises.strong: Use the API endpoint to create users in the database.
writing_improvement_exercises.lesson: Avoid unnecessary jargon and buzzwords. Say what you mean simply.

writing_improvement_exercises.title: Be Specific
writing_improvement_exercises.weak: The system performs well under high load.
writing_improvement_exercises.strong: The system handles 10,000 requests per second with p95 latency under 100ms.
writing_improvement_exercises.lesson: Quantify performance claims with specific metrics.
